import math
import pytest
from humanize.number import (
    ordinal,
    intcomma,
    intword,
    apnumber,
    fractional,
    scientific,
    clamp,
    metric,
)


def test_ordinal_non_finite():
    assert ordinal(float("nan")) == "NaN"
    assert ordinal(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert ordinal(float("inf")) == "+Inf"


def test_ordinal_non_int_convertible():
    # string that cannot be turned into an int
    assert ordinal("something else") == "something else"
    # list is not numeric
    assert ordinal([1, 2, 3]) == "[1, 2, 3]"


def test_ordinal_gender_parameter():
    # gender does not affect the suffix in the default (English) locale
    assert ordinal(1, gender="male") == "1st"
    assert ordinal(1, gender="female") == "1st"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# intcomma
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,ndigits,expected",
    [
        (100, None, "100"),
        ("1000", None, "1,000"),
        (1_000_000, None, "1,000,000"),
        (1_234_567.25, None, "1,234,567.25"),
        (1234.5454545, 2, "1,234.55"),
        (14308.40, 1, "14,308.4"),
        ("14308.40", 1, "14,308.4"),
    ],
)
def test_intcomma_normal(value, ndigits, expected):
    assert intcomma(value, ndigits) == expected


def test_intcomma_none_and_non_finite():
    assert intcomma(None) == "None"
    assert intcomma(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert intcomma(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert intcomma(float("nan")) == "NaN"


def test_intcomma_invalid_input():
    # a value that cannot be parsed as a number
    class Bad:
        def __str__(self):
            return "bad"

    assert intcomma(Bad()) == "bad"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# intword
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,expected",
    [
        ("100", "100"),
        ("12400", "12.4 thousand"),
        (1_200_000_000, "1.2 billion"),
        (10**33, "1.0 decillion"),
    ],
)
def test_intword_normal(value, expected):
    assert intword(value) == expected


def test_intword_negative():
    assert intword(-1500) == "-1.5 thousand"


def test_intword_custom_format():
    assert intword("1234000", "%0.3f") == "1.234 million"


def test_intword_non_finite_and_invalid():
    assert intword(float("nan")) == "NaN"
    assert intword(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert intword(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert intword("foo") == "foo"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# apnumber
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,expected",
    [
        (0, "zero"),
        (5, "five"),
        (10, "10"),
        ("7", "seven"),
        ("foo", "foo"),
        (None, "None"),
    ],
)
def test_apnumber_basic(value, expected):
    assert apnumber(value) == expected


def test_apnumber_non_finite():
    assert apnumber(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert apnumber(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert apnumber(float("nan")) == "NaN"


def test_apnumber_negative_out_of_range():
    # -1 is not in 0‑9, should be returned as string
    assert apnumber(-1) == "-1"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# fractional
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,expected",
    [
        (0.3, "3/10"),
        (1.3, "1 3/10"),
        (float(1 / 3), "1/3"),
        (1, "1"),
        ("ten", "ten"),
        (None, "None"),
        (-0.25, "-1/4"),
        (-1.3, "-1 3/10"),
    ],
)
def test_fractional_cases(value, expected):
    assert fractional(value) == expected


def test_fractional_non_finite():
    assert fractional(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert fractional(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert fractional(float("nan")) == "NaN"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# scientific
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,precision,expected",
    [
        (0.3, 2, "3.00 x 10⁻¹"),
        (500, 2, "5.00 x 10²"),
        (-1000, 2, "-1.00 x 10³"),
        (1000, 1, "1.0 x 10³"),
        (1000, 3, "1.000 x 10³"),
        ("99", 2, "9.90 x 10¹"),
        (1, 2, "1.00 x 10⁰"),
    ],
)
def test_scientific_normal(value, precision, expected):
    assert scientific(value, precision) == expected


def test_scientific_invalid_and_non_finite():
    assert scientific("foo") == "foo"
    assert scientific(None) == "None"
    assert scientific(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert scientific(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert scientific(float("nan")) == "NaN"


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# clamp
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def test_clamp_no_limits():
    assert clamp(123.456) == "123.456"


def test_clamp_floor():
    assert clamp(0.0001, floor=0.01) == "<0.01"


def test_clamp_ceil_exact_and_exceed():
    assert clamp(0.99, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) == "99%"
    assert clamp(0.999, format="{:.0%}", ceil=0.99) == ">99%"


def test_clamp_callable_format():
    result = clamp(1, format=intword, floor=1e6, floor_token="under ")
    assert result == "under 1.0 million"


def test_clamp_none_and_non_finite():
    assert clamp(None) is None
    assert clamp(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert clamp(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert clamp(float("nan")) == "NaN"


def test_clamp_invalid_format():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        clamp(1, format=123)  # not a string nor callable


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# metric
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "value,unit,precision,expected",
    [
        (1500, "V", 3, "1.50 kV"),
        (2e8, "W", 3, "200 MW"),
        (220e-6, "F", 3, "220 μF"),
        (1e-14, "", 4, "10.00 f"),
        (0, "", 3, "0.00"),
        (-1500, "", 3, "-1.50 k"),
    ],
)
def test_metric_normal(value, unit, precision, expected):
    assert metric(value, unit, precision) == expected


def test_metric_extreme_exponents():
    # exponent >= 33 -> scientific fallback
    assert metric(1e40) == "1.00 x 10⁴⁰"
    # exponent < -30 -> scientific fallback
    assert metric(1e-35) == "1.00 x 10⁻³⁵"


def test_metric_non_finite():
    assert metric(float("inf")) == "+Inf"
    assert metric(float("-inf")) == "-Inf"
    assert metric(float("nan")) == "NaN"
